main_body: A steel column: a wide rounded cap with rivets at the top, a ribbed shaft with horizontal bands, and a base drum that mirrors the cap.
top_band: Light steel L=172 at rows 9-11 (3 rows), a highlight line at row 12 (L=210), then 1 row at row 13 and a dark underside at rows 14-16. The cap stays in one lightness family from row 9 to 13, so it reads as a front-on banded drum.
evidence: The cap is wider than the shaft with rounded corners, but rows 9-13 form one light family with rivet dots on rows 12-13. That reads as the face of a drum seen from the front, not a top ellipse. Only about 3 rows are plausibly a top, and the row-12 highlight is more likely a band line than a front edge. The shaft is a flat vertical elevation with ribs painted on and no recess. The base repeats the same banded pattern. In doubt, so fail.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. 95% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a near-black sticker line, while the references use tinted outlines (1% and 33% neutral). It has about 5 flat lightness steps and no per-material texture or grain. It is much thinner than the references and looks more sticker-like.
